title: Connection hold/resume negotiation and tool-call ACK safeguards
author: Maya Kapoor
description: Summary: Adds a connection 'hold' state and deterministic resume negotiation to reduce spurious session aborts on transient client disconnects and to ensure ordered, idempotent tool/function calls after reconnect. Also introduces an explicit server-enforced soft-timeout for passive streams and an ACK gating mechanism so tool-calls are only committed once the client has acknowledged sufficient progress. Motivation: In production we've observed two classes of failures: 1) brief client network interruptions cause immediate session tombstoning causing loss of in-flight tool calls and confusing clients; 2) dual-path commit races where the server retries or replays tool/function calls after reconnect, causing duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent tools. This PR implements a protocol-level negotiator to keep sessions in a hold/quarantine state during short disconnects, a deterministic resume handshake to reconcile in-flight operations and KV cache offsets, and an ACK gating rule to defer tool-call finalization until the client confirms receipt of stable progress. Design: 1) New state machine: ACTIVE -> HOLD -> RESUME_NEGOTIATION -> ACTIVE or EVICT. HOLD is entered on TCP/websocket disconnect or prolonged socket stall; it prevents immediate tombstoning and continues short-lived resource reservation. 2) Resume negotiation: client re-connect includes a resume token + last-ack-offset; server reconciles inflight queue, deduplicates tool-calls using run-id + sequence, and returns an explicit commit plan. 3) Tool-call ACK gating: tool integrations now accept provisional execution IDs; final side-effect commit only proceeds after a client ACK or when a server soft-timeout elapses with conservative hedging. 4) Soft-timeout: default 45s soft hold timeout for passive streams; configurable per-customer tier and override via Dedicated/Private policies. 5) OpenAI compatibility layer: stream adapter updated to expose resume semantics via the same SSE/websocket boundaries while preserving existing top-level API surface. Backwards compatibility: existing clients that do not send resume tokens will see unchanged behavior (server falls back to previous eviction rules). New ACK gating is opt-in via a request-level header X-Redwood-ack-mode=provisional which defaults to off for older SDKs. Implementation notes: - runtime/streaming/negotiator.py: new state machine and reconciliation code. - api/openai_compat/stream_adapter.go: updated handshake and resume flow mapping to the OpenAI streaming model. - sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py and sdk/typescript/...: client helpers to emit resume tokens and manage provisional tool call lifecycle. - hooks added to observability to surface hold-duration histograms and resume outcome counts. Testing and validation: unit tests for state transitions and deduplication logic added (tests/unit/test_negotiator.py). Integration tests simulating flaky networks and duplicate tool-call scenarios (tests/integration/test_stream_resume.py). Load bench locally showed median additional CPU <2% for streams under normal traffic. Rollout plan: Feature gated under runtime flag stream_resume_negotiator_v1, will be enabled for internal E2E only, then staged to Canary customers (low-traffic tenants), after 2 weeks open for all Hosted, then included in Dedicated/Private release notes with config knobs. Observability: new metrics: stream.hold_duration_ms, stream.resume_outcome{success,merge,eject}, toolcall.commit_lag_ms, toolcall.duplicate_detected_count. Migration and operator actions: Dedicated/Private operators may override soft-timeout via deployment config; documented in docs/streaming/hold_resume.md.
